message.content:
Below are two ways you can provision a **Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000** GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> ⚠️ **Important** – Google Cloud does not use the “EC2” terminology; that’s Amazon Web Services.  
> In GCP the equivalent service is **Compute Engine**.  
> The examples below assume you already have a GCP project, billing enabled, and the Compute Engine API turned on.

---

## 1️⃣  gcloud CLI (recommended)

```bash
# 1. Authenticate (once per session)
gcloud auth login
gcloud config set project YOUR_PROJECT_ID
gcloud config set compute/zone us-central1-a   # pick your preferred zone

# 2. Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --machine-type n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM (adjust as needed)
  --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --image-family ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size 100GB \
  --boot-disk-type pd-ssd \
  --maintenance-policy TERMINATE \        # optional: how to handle maintenance events
  --scopes cloud-platform \               # optional: grant full access
  --metadata startup-script='#!/bin/bash
    # Install NVIDIA driver (GPU drivers are not pre‑installed)
    sudo apt-get update
    sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
    sudo reboot'
```

### What this does

| Parameter | Meaning |
|-----------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds one RTX A6000 (`nvidia-tesla-a6000`). |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Uses the official Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` / `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk of 100 GB. |
| `startup-script` | Installs the NVIDIA driver automatically on first boot. |

> **Tip:** If you need more GPUs or a different machine type, adjust the `--machine-type` and `--accelerator` flags accordingly.

---

## 2️⃣  REST API (curl)

If you prefer to use the raw REST API, here’s a minimal example.  
You’ll need an OAuth 2.0 access token with the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform` scope.

```bash
# 1. Get an access token (replace YOUR_CLIENT_ID/YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET if you’re using a service account)
export ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

# 2. Prepare the JSON payload
cat <<EOF > instance.json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\\napt-get update\\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535\\nreboot"
      }
    ]
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ]
}
EOF

# 3. POST the request
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json
```

### Explanation of the JSON fields

| Field | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `name` | Instance name. |
| `machineType` | Full URL to the machine type. |
| `disks[0]` | Boot disk configuration (Ubuntu image, 100 GB SSD). |
| `accelerators[0]` | Adds one RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `metadata.items[0]` | Startup script that installs the NVIDIA driver. |
| `serviceAccounts[0]` | Grants the instance full Cloud Platform access. |

> **Note:** The `acceleratorType` URL includes the zone (`us-central1-a`).  
> If you’re using a different zone, replace it accordingly.

---

## 🚀 Quick Checklist

1. **Project & Billing** – Ensure the project exists and billing is enabled.  
2. **API Enabled** – `Compute Engine API` must be turned on.  
3. **GPU Quota** – Verify you have enough GPU quota in the chosen zone.  
4. **Driver Installation** – The startup script installs the NVIDIA driver; you can customize it further if needed.  
5. **Firewall Rules** – If you need external access (SSH, RDP, etc.), make sure the appropriate firewall rules are in place.

Happy GPU computing! 🚀
